newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-No deal at Australian Premiers Conference.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-No deal at Australian Premiers Conference.

text.p: The Australian Premiers Conference on Friday failed to produce its annual fiscal arrangement between the federal and state governments.

"This is the first Premiers Conference in the history of federation that has adjourned without an agreement between the Commonwealth (federal government) and the States," New South Wales Treasurer Michael Egan told reporters.

The federal government had made no concrete proposal in the morning discussions and then after lunch had suddenly demanded cuts in federal funding to the states worth A$410 million in real terms, Egan said.
Egan, speaking for the state and territory treasurers, said they had made their contribution to repairing the federal government's fiscal problems last year.
"We got here today to be told that another A$410 million is to be cut from our specific-purpose payments," he said.
That amount represented a three percent cut in real terms.
The states do not levy income tax and therefore rely on federal money, the level of which is determined at the annual Premiers Conference, which is invariably acrimonious.
The federal government pays them under two broad headings -- general grants, which the states can spend as they please, and specific-purpose grants, which must be spent as Canberra says.

Although the specific-purpose payments serve federal government priorities, they are still crucial to the states, because they cover areas that would otherwise have to be topped up with money from other sources.
Egan said the reductions in specific-purpose grants would force savage cuts in state services.
"We are prepared to come back at some stage and reassemble after going back to our states," Egan said.
Last year Canberra, looking for savings to repair a federal budget deep in deficit, cut the state's specific-purpose payments by about A$500 million.
The states then also agreed to contribute three annual lump sums to Canberra's fiscal repair programme by sacrificing A$1.5 billion of their general grants in the three fiscal years to June 1999.
Queensland Treasurer Joan Sheldon said: "We either put up taxes, cut services or do both. We are not prepared to do either."
Egan said Prime Minister John Howard and federal Treasurer Peter Costello had not agreed among themselves in the meeting.
"One was saying one thing and the other was saying the other," he said.
Costello's office was not available for comment.
The federal government cut its budget by A$7 billion last year, including the lower funding to the states.
In January, Costello said the budget was in worse shape than previously thought and more cuts, worth A$2 billion to A$4 billion in a full fiscal year, would be needed.
